memory_update.text: SCCO and FCX should remain reference anchors for the sulphuric-acid/SX-EW node because filings directly connect sulfuric acid use or production to copper leaching.
CGIFF/CHE.UN is the best underfollowed direct acid-supply candidate found in this pass; next layer should quantify mining/metals customer exposure and contract repricing sensitivity.

GCUMF/GCU.V is a below-USD-300M speculative exception with unusually direct node relevance through SX-EW and planned sulfur-burning acid production, but survival depends on financing, permitting, sulfur sourcing, and execution evidence.

The node may reward acid-integrated copper producers and merchant acid/logistics providers while pressuring acid-import-dependent HPAL and SX-EW operators; this remains a hypothesis until company-level acid cost and availability disclosures confirm impact.

Need a follow-up search for US-listed or OTC public owners of sulphur terminals, acid tank storage, smelter-acid exporters, and Chile/Indonesia acid logistics routes; many relevant assets may sit inside Japanese trading houses, private traders, or non-US listings.

node: Sulphur and sulphuric-acid feedstock for copper SX-EW and nickel HPAL
summary: Expanded the direct public-company universe around the sulphur/sulphuric-acid chokepoint into two lanes: reference copper producers with material SX-EW or acid integration, and underfollowed public acid/sulphur-chain names whose relevance may be hidden by chemical-logistics or junior-miner labels. The strongest direct exposure in this pass is not AI or battery OEMs, but copper leach operators, smelter-acid producers, and sulphuric-acid logistics/producers. Key uncertainty: whether the 2026 acid/sulphur disruption is temporary trade-route stress or a durable structural constraint that changes realized margins, customer behavior, or project economics.
